title: XOR tricks
summary: x ^ x = 0 and x ^ 0 = x, so XOR-ing everything cancels pairs. Single number, missing number, swap without a temp, and finding two unique numbers.

sections.title: Properties
sections.body:
✍️ `x ^ x = 0`, `x ^ 0 = x`, XOR is commutative and associative (order does not matter).
✍️ So XOR-ing a list where every value appears twice except one leaves exactly that one value. O(n) time, O(1) space.

sections.title: Single number
Missing number
sections.body: ✍️ XOR all indices 0..n and all values: every present number cancels with its index, the missing one remains. (Or sum formula n(n+1)/2 − sum.)

sections.title: Two numbers appear once (LeetCode 260)
sections.body: XOR everything → `x = a ^ b` (non-zero). Pick any set bit of x (`x & −x`): a and b differ there. Split all numbers by that bit and XOR each group separately → a and b.

sections.title: Pitfalls
sections.body: ✍️ XOR only cancels **pairs**. "Every element appears three times except one" (LeetCode 137) needs per-bit counting mod 3.
